newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE INJURY FORCES ENGLAND RESHUFFLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE INJURY FORCES ENGLAND RESHUFFLE.

text.p: England coach Jack Rowell was forced to shelve a number of experiments on Thursday after new captain Phil de Glanville was ruled out of Saturday's test against Argentina.
De Glanville has suffered a leg strain and becomes the third unavailable member of the England back-line for the final pre-Christmas test of the season.
Full-back Tim Stimpson and wing Adedayo Adebayo were already missing with concussion, and Rowell's plans will be further complicated if fly-half Mike Catt does not recover from a chest complaint.
Prop Jason Leonard takes over the captaincy, Jeremy Guscott is restored to the centre having been originally selected on the wing and Northampton fly-half Paul Grayson has been added to the squad.

If Grayson ends up playing, England will ironically be left with a backline containing three players axed by Rowell in the quest for a more potent back division, plus ex-captain Will Carling whose place has been under increasing threat since De Glanville was named as his successor.
The reshuffle at least gives winger Tony Underwood the chance to resume an international career rudely interrupted by Jonah Lomu in the World Cup 18 months ago.
It also re-unites Carling and Guscott whose world record 43 appearances together in the England midfield seemed to have ended with equal abruptness after De Glanville's appointment.
"It would have been Phil's third game as England captain and we were looking forward to him leading England in the direction we have been playing," said Rowell.
"We lost two people with concussion last weekend and could have done without anyone else being removed because two changes were enough and the team was evolving encouragingly.
"But Jerry and Will now have the chance to show us the chemistry of a centre pairing which was interrupte."
For Argentina, attempting to atone for a 51-0 defeat on their last visit to Twickenham in 1990, the changes amongst the opposition do not alter their long-term goals.
"There are very big changes happening in Argentine rugby," said captain Lisandro Arbizu."We want to play another type of rugby and we're hoping to show it on Saturday."
